Title: IS Acquisition and Development
Summary: The core focus of this chapter, covering project management, development methodologies, and controls.

Title: Definition and Scope
Summary: Defined policies and procedures used to plan, execute, and control IS projects.

Title: Organizational Framework
Summary: Organizational framework defining how project teams interact and report.

Title: Duty Definition
Summary: Clear definition of duties for all personnel involved in the project.

Title: Common Tools and Methods
Summary: Tools and methods like PERT, Gantt charts, or critical path analysis.

Title: Portfolio Oversight
Summary: Strategic selection of projects aligned with organizational goals (portfolio).

Title: Program Oversight
Summary: Oversight of multiple related projects (program).

Title: Function and Standardization
Summary: Centralized department that standardizes project governance and processes.

Title: Value Assurance
Summary: Ensuring the project delivers the intended business value and measurable outcomes.

Title: Formal Start
Summary: The formal process of starting a new project or phase.

Title: SMART Goals
Summary: Specific, measurable, achievable, relevant, and time-bound goals for the project.

Title: Project Planning
Summary: Developing the project management plan, scope, schedule, and resource allocation.

Title: Schedule Development
Summary: The process of determining task sequences and durations.

Title: Gantt Chart Creation (L4 Example)
Summary: A specific tool used for visualizing the project timeline and dependencies.

Title: Task Implementation
Summary: Carrying out the planned tasks and producing the deliverables.

Title: Performance Tracking
Summary: Tracking, reviewing, and regulating the progress and performance of the project.

Title: Formal Completion
Summary: Formal completion of the project, including delivery, review, and documentation.

Title: Defining Boundaries
Summary: The boundaries and limits of the project, defining what is and is not included (scope management).

Title: System Assessment
Summary: Assessment of the existing system or process to identify weaknesses and opportunities.

Title: Functional Requirements
Summary: Detailed needs describing what the system must do.

Title: Non-Functional Requirements
Summary: Detailed constraints on how the system must perform (e.g., security, performance, reliability).

Title: Development Strategy
Summary: The planned method or strategy for system development (e.g., in-house, purchase, outsourcing).

Title: Alternative Analysis
Summary: Analyzing costs, benefits, and risks across different solution alternatives.

Title: Business Case Approval
Summary: Formal assessment of the business case before approval to proceed.

Title: Software Creation
Summary: The process of creating software or applications to meet specific business needs.

Title: Framework Examples
Summary: Different frameworks for system development, such as Waterfall, Agile, or V-model.

Title: Sequential Steps
Summary: Sequential steps in the System Development Life Cycle (e.g., Planning, Analysis, Design, Implementation, Maintenance).

Title: Coding and Testing Techniques
Summary: Specific techniques used in coding and testing, like object-oriented programming or structured programming.

Title: System Development Tools and Productivity Aids
Efficiency Tools
Summary: CASE tools, code generators, debuggers, and other tools that enhance development efficiency.

Title: Planning and Design
Summary: The process of planning, designing, and acquiring the necessary hardware, network, and operating systems.

Title: Procurement and Testing
Summary: Procedures for procurement, testing, and implementation of new technology components.

Title: Foundational Software
Summary: Acquiring operating systems, database management systems, and other foundational software.

Title: Data Capture and Authorization
Summary: Controls ensuring data is accurately captured and authorized at the source (e.g., validation checks, sequence checks).

Title: Data Integrity in Processing
Summary: Controls ensuring data is correctly processed (e.g., batch totals, cross-footing, limit checks).

Title: Accuracy, Security, and Distribution
Summary: Controls ensuring output is accurate, secure, and delivered only to authorized recipients (e.g., review procedures, reconciliation).

Title: Embedded Software Controls
Summary: Controls embedded within the application software itself to ensure data integrity and security (e.g., access controls, audit trails).

Title: Manual Operations and Policies
Summary: Manual steps and policies users follow to operate the system securely and correctly.

Title: Data Quality and Model Controls
Summary: System designed to support decision-making activities, often requiring specific controls over data quality and models.
